solution.concept: The vector equation of a line passing through a point with position vector 'a' and parallel to a vector 'b' is given by r = a + λb, where λ is a scalar parameter. The Cartesian equation of a line passing through a point (x₁, y₁, z₁) and having direction ratios a, b, c is (x - x₁)/a = (y - y₁)/b = (z - z₁)/c. Its vector form is r = (x₁i + y₁j + z₁k) + λ(ai + bj + ck). The direction cosines of the x-axis, y-axis, and z-axis are (1, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0), and (0, 0, 1) respectively. If a line has direction ratios a, b, c, then its direction cosines l, m, n are given by l = a / √(a² + b² + c²), m = b / √(a² + b² + c²), n = c / √(a² + b² + c²). A line has two sets of direction cosines, (l, m, n) and (-l, -m, -n), corresponding to the two opposite directions along the line.
